newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares off lows, end down 2.91 pct on Thai woes.
newsitem.headline: KL shares off lows, end down 2.91 pct on Thai woes.

text.p: Shares closed off lows on afternoon bargain hunting after falling to a 16-month low as both institutional and retail investors dumped stock.
The key Composite Index closed down 31.22 points or 2.91 percent to 1,041.27, after falling as low as 1,024.19, the lowest since January 19 last year when it hit 1,021.92.
Most Asian markets also were lower.

The plunge was accompanied by rumours that large foreign investment banks were calling to downgrade Malaysia. This talk was triggered by fears that economic woes in Thailand may infect other nations of the region.
A weak economic growth, coupled with a property market crisis in Thailand has led to a review of financial markets in the Philippines, Malaysia and Singapore, the brokers said.
The all main-board Emas Index fell 8.91 points or 2.91 percent to 297.23.
The rebound was helped by views that the market was oversold. "This is definitely an oversold position," said a senior equity salesman at a Japanese bank in Singapore.
But he warned that "an oversold market can remain oversold for a long time like Thailand."
